items.title: Inbox triage searches unread mail without an age window, so a missed slot cannot lose mail
items.why: The hourly triage searches `newer_than:3h`; when slots are missed (GitHub cron gaps 2026-09-21/22, usage limits) the mail in between is never read. Nine unread threads dated 2026-09-18..21 surfaced only on 2026-09-28 17:07 by a manual catch-up (docs/INBOX.md 'Backlog catch-up'): the Gmail Send-as confirmation for info@gankdat.com (expired unclicked, owner had to redo it), Chrome Web Store identity verification (publishing unblocked a week late), the mcpservers.org approval, the Datarade application receipt. Fix: replace the search with `in:inbox is:unread` (no age filter) and mark each logged thread read in the same run (already done for triaged mail), so the window is the read state, not the clock; cap one run at 30 threads, oldest first, and note 'backlog' in the INBOX line when the mail is older than 3 h. Exact sentence for the triage prompt: 'Search Gmail for `in:inbox is:unread` (no newer_than filter): unread is the queue, so a missed slot only delays mail; process oldest first, at most 30 threads per run, mark each processed thread read, and write `(backlog)` after the timestamp of any thread older than 3 h.' Prompt edit is a handoff. Evidence 3 (9 threads, two owner-visible consequences) × reach 2 ÷ 0.1 days. Built 2026-09-30 (fallback): docs/routines/inbox-triage.md step 1 now reads the exact sentence above and step 2 carries the `(backlog)` marker; docs/SCHEDULERS.md names the new window. The live prompt replacement rides the existing 2026-09-29 ALERTS handoff (the routine was created via the HTTP API, so update_trigger refuses agents), which now covers both triage sentences in one edit.
items.proof: no 'backlog' or 'found unread' INBOX line over 30 days; every store mail logged within 2 h of arrival

items.title: Fallback routine detects a late Fable slot, not just a missed one, before it starts building
items.why: Today the 09:00 Fable build committed at 09:28, 8 minutes after the 09:20 fallback had run its STEP 0 check and concluded the slot was missed. Both built, and the push collided: a merge conflict in queues/foundry.json that had to be resolved by hand (this run kept both sides; a less careful resolution loses one routine's work). The check can only see a slot that has already committed, so any Fable run slower than 20 minutes triggers the same race, twice a day. Options for the fix: have the build routine write a `| build | started` run-log line (or a docs/ops/RUNNING lock file) at the top of its run so the fallback can see an in-flight slot; or move the fallback to +45 min; or have the fallback re-check immediately before its commit and rebase rather than merge. Cheapest is the started-line: one sentence in the build prompt, one check in the fallback prompt. SECOND OCCURRENCE the same day (evidence, not a new item): the 17:00 Fable build committed at 17:29:57, 9 minutes after the 17:20 fallback's STEP 0 check, and both built the SAME item (self-caused-alerts) — the fallback's duplicate was discarded on merge, so a whole Opus slot produced only the closure work Fable had left undone. Twice in one day now; the check cannot see a slot that has not committed yet. THIRD OCCURRENCE 2026-09-30 (evidence, not a new item): the 09:00 Fable build committed at 09:27:37, six minutes after the 09:21 STEP 0 check, so every collision so far has been inside a 6-9 minute window after the check. This one cost no duplicated work — Fable took gankdat `claude-directory-listing` and the fallback a foundry item — but still produced the same three-file merge conflict (ALERTS, RUNS, STRATEGY, all end-of-file appends) resolved by hand. Three collisions in two days across both slots; a started-line or lock the fallback can read before STEP 0 is the only option that closes the window, since moving the fallback later only moves it. BUILT 2026-09-30 (burn-down): scripts/slot.ts — `npm run slot -- start build` appends `- YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM | build | started` to docs/ops/SLOTS.md and pushes commit `build: slot … UTC started (build)` as the run's first action (before npm ci), which the fallback's existing '(build) commit in the last 2 h' check already stops on, so no fallback prompt change is required; `npm run slot -- check build` prints running/done/missed. The run watchdog never takes the marker for the work and reports a stamped-then-dead slot as `stalled:`. The instruction is in CLAUDE.md (loaded by every session) so it applies from the next build; the exact prompt sentence rides the open 2026-09-29 prompt handoff in ALERTS. Exercised live on this run's own slot (commit 568e2f4).
items.proof: no second collision over 30 days: no merge conflict between a build and a fallback commit, and no day with both a `(build)` and a `(fallback)` commit inside 30 minutes

items.title: Store metrics job in CI: a script reads every STORE.md's listing URLs from a GitHub runner and writes the Daily check row itself (CWS page, AMO API, Figma API)
items.why: The Sonnet metrics routine cannot reach the stores from its sandbox ('fetch failed: egress blocked by network policy (chromewebstore.google.com, addons.mozilla.org)', highlight-keep RESEARCH 2026-09-21) and, since it reads STORE.md's status line for whether to try, has written 'not live yet' for read-focus and highlight-keep every day 2026-09-20..30 while all four of their listings were live: AMO approved both on 2026-09-22 (found 2026-09-30 via relay amo-listings, API status public, ReadFocus 2 weekly downloads) and the Chrome Web Store pages both answer 200 with a slug redirect and an 'Add to Chrome' button (relay cws-status/cws-pages 2026-09-30; no approval mail ever reached INBOX.md, so the triage-driven fix store-approval-to-store-md alone would not have caught it). Ten days of a launched product with no reading, twice. The gankdat metrics already run this way (gankdat-metrics.yml → scripts/metrics.mjs from a runner with egress). Fix: scripts/store-metrics.mjs run by docs/ci/store-metrics.yml daily 06:45: for each ventures/*/STORE.md parse the listing URLs; CWS: GET the detail page and read the user count and rating from the page's structured data (a 404 or no 'Add to Chrome' = not live); AMO: GET api/v5/addons/addon/<slug>/ (average_daily_users, weekly_downloads, ratings); Figma: the community API the metrics routine already uses via relay (relay metrics-2026-09-25); append one 'Daily check' row per venture to its RESEARCH.md and flip a STORE.md 'not live yet' to live with the date when the page answers — then the Sonnet routine only reads. Evidence 3 (4 listings unread for 8-10 days, 2 ventures, review W39 and report W40 both flagged it) × reach 3 (every non-gankdat venture, daily; review; report) ÷ 0.3 days. Built 2026-09-30 burn-down: scripts/store-metrics.ts (19 tests) + docs/ci/store-metrics.yml (06:45 daily + on push, fills missing rows only); a dry run against the relay bodies produced the real 2026-09-30 rows for read-focus and highlight-keep, which replaced the day's 'not live yet' rows in the same commit. First live push run (19:48): Chrome and Firefox read from the runner, Figma answered 403 to the script's own agent — fixed the same run with the relay's browser-shaped agent, and an unreadable page now writes 'unread', never 'not live yet'.

items.title: Deterministic Taskmaster row: scripts/taskmaster-add.ts appends a task to .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json without the MCP or the AI CLI, so routines stop filing Taskmaster handoffs
items.why: gankdat's CLAUDE.md wants a Taskmaster task before a new module, but no routine can create one: the task-master-ai MCP times out at session start in every cloud sandbox (CONNECT_TIMEOUT 2026-09-21, 22, 23, 24, 29, 30 ×2 — ALERTS handoffs, 14 mentions in ALERTS.md), the sandbox has no task-master CLI, and `npx -y task-master-ai --version` crashes in the sandbox with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (zod/v4, tested 2026-09-30). Four modules (metrics-change-feed-count, claude-directory-listing, mcp-oauth-lazy-auth, the OAuth migration) are waiting on one handoff for rows that need no AI at all: tasks.json is plain JSON ({master:{tasks:[{id,title,description,status,priority,dependencies,details,testStrategy,subtasks}],metadata}}). Fix: scripts/taskmaster-add.ts (`npm run task -- add --title … --description … --details … [--status done]`) that validates the shape, takes the next id, sets metadata.lastModified/taskCount/completedCount, and regenerates nothing else (task-master generate is optional); plus a `task -- done <id>` verb. The routine prompts' 'file a Taskmaster row' step then works offline; the open handoff rows get filed by the first build that runs it. Evidence 3 (seven occurrences, every gankdat module) × reach 2 (build, fallback, burn-down) ÷ 0.15 days. Built 2026-09-30 burn-down: scripts/taskmaster-add.ts (`npm run task -- add|status|done|list`, 8 tests, validates the tag shape, next id, metadata counts); the three open handoff rows (17, 18, 19) were filed with it in the same commit and both CLAUDE.md files point at the offline form.
items.proof: zero Taskmaster handoffs in ALERTS.md over 30 days; every gankdat module shipped after this has its tasks.json row in the same commit

items.title: Routine prompts live in the repo: each stored prompt becomes a three-line bootstrap that reads docs/routines/<name>.md, so a prompt change is a commit instead of a handoff
items.why: Routines cannot edit their own prompts (update_trigger refuses triggers created via the HTTP API, 2026-09-29), so every prompt fix waits for the interactive session: the 2026-09-29 handoff now carries three triage sentences and one report sentence (self-caused-alerts, triage-backlog-window, store-approval-to-store-md), a fourth handoff of 2026-09-30 carries the build routine's slot-start sentence, and the ops retro has been disabled since 2026-09-26 waiting for its repository attach. Four prompt changes in two days, all queued behind one person; meanwhile the routines already follow repo text without a handoff (CLAUDE.md is loaded into every session, which is how fallback-slot-race shipped). Fix: one last handoff per routine that replaces the stored prompt with: 'You are the Foundry <name> routine. Run `git fetch origin && git checkout main && git pull` (on unrelated histories: `git switch -c work origin/main`, push with `git push origin HEAD:main`), then read `docs/routines/<name>.md` on that branch and do exactly what it says. Never touch .env, never create accounts or spend money.' The mirrors under docs/routines/ become the prompts of record (triage, report and retro already exist; build, burn-down, exchange, review and metrics need writing from the live prompts — the burn-down text is in hand from its own run; the others are read from claude.ai/code/routines by the interactive session). Security posture unchanged: the repo already steers every run through CLAUDE.md. Evidence 3 (five prompt handoffs in two days, one routine dark four days) × reach 3 (all eight routines, forever) ÷ 0.3 days (mirrors + one handoff listing all eight replacements). Built 2026-09-30 burn-down: docs/routines/README.md (bootstrap text, trigger table, provenance and editing rules); burn-down.md verbatim from the running prompt; build.md, fallback.md, exchange.md, review.md, metrics.md written from the repo record with the queued sentences folded in (the interactive session reconciles each against the stored text before swapping); the three existing mirrors relabelled prompts of record; one ALERTS handoff replaces the three open prompt handoffs; CLAUDE.md, SCHEDULERS.md and OPERATIONS.md name the mechanism.
items.proof: zero prompt-change handoffs in ALERTS.md over 30 days after the switch; a prompt change lands in the next scheduled run of that routine

items.title: CI jobs that diff the push range check out full depth: a two-commit push no longer crashes notify-owner or blinds the Apify publish job
items.why: notify-owner run 63 (2026-09-30 19:57, push 587a3d9..139b7e9) failed with `fatal: Invalid revision range`: the job checks out `fetch-depth: 2` while DIFF_RANGE is `github.event.before..sha`, so any push carrying two or more commits (the burn-down pushed 18ec948 and 139b7e9 within a minute, GitHub coalesced them) has no `before` commit locally. The first diff swallowed the error and returned nothing, the second crashed — the four 19:56 run bullets never reached the owner's phone and the job went red. gankdat-publish.yml has the same depth and range: on a coalesced push its `git diff --name-only` would crash before any actor is priced or published. Fix: `fetch-depth: 0` in both workflows (the repo is 22 MB) via docs/ci/, and both scripts fall back to `HEAD~1..HEAD` with a printed notice when the range does not resolve (branch creation, force-push) instead of throwing. Evidence 2 (one loss, both jobs exposed on every multi-commit push — the burn-down's hourly runs make those common) × reach 3 (every owner notification and every actor publish) ÷ 0.05 days.
items.proof: zero notify-owner or gankdat-publish failures with `Invalid revision range` over 30 days; every burn-down RUNS line arrives as a Telegram bullet

items.title: A dataset that errors on refresh two days running becomes a scored gankdat queue item automatically, written by the 06:30 metrics job
items.why: uk-insolvency has been in the Daily numbers `refresh errors` field four days running (2026-09-27 500, 09-28 `Unexpected end of JSON input`, 09-29 500, 09-30 `page results-page=1: Unexpected end of JSON input after 3 reads (0 bytes, content-length declared)`), and uk-charities and uk-trademark-journal logged `D1_ERROR: Network connection lost` on 09-28; the 09-29 build fixed only the 500 case (`gazette-5xx-retry`) because a routine only sees the row it happens to read, and no queue item exists for the live failure — the surface serves a stale insolvency snapshot while the gankdat queue holds nothing buildable. Fix: `ventures/gankdat/scripts/metrics.mjs` (runs in CI with the D1 numbers) compares today's error slugs with yesterday's row; a slug present both days gets an idempotent `todo` item `refresh-<slug>` in `docs/pipeline/queues/gankdat.json` (score 6, effort 0.1, the two messages in `why`, evidence appended on later days, never re-added once done or dropped within 14 days) in the same metrics commit, so `npm run pipeline next` offers it to the next build. Evidence 3 (one dataset broken four days, three slugs in a week, nobody queued it) × reach 3 (all 17 datasets, every day) ÷ 0.1 days. Built 2026-09-30 burn-down: scripts/refresh-errors-to-queue.ts (`npm run refresh-errors`, 7 tests: nested-comma parsing, both-days rule, extend-once, 14-day cool-off, unique re-file id) runs in the metrics job after metrics.mjs (docs/ci/gankdat-metrics.yml, the commit step adds the queue file); dry run on today's rows filed refresh-uk-insolvency, which the research item of the same evening now carries.

items.title: notify-owner sends everything since a committed cursor instead of the push range, so a failed job's bullets go out on the next push
items.why: When notify-owner run 63 crashed (2026-09-30 19:57, `push-diff-range-depth`), the four RUNS bullets of that push were lost for good: the job diffs `github.event.before..sha` and nothing ever looks at that range again — the same holds for a Telegram 5xx, a runner loss or a red `check` that cancels the job. Fix: the job reads `docs/ops/NOTIFIED.md` (the last RUNS/ALERTS line hashes it sent), sends every newer `owner:` line and RUNS line, and commits the new cursor with `[skip ci]` only after Telegram answered 2xx; a failure leaves the cursor where it was and the next push (the watchdog pushes hourly at worst) resends. Evidence 2 (one loss today; every earlier failed run — 2026-09-24, 09-28 red-CI pushes — lost its bullets the same way) × reach 3 (every owner notification) ÷ 0.1 days. Built 2026-09-30 (burn-down): `scripts/notify-owner.ts` (14 tests) replaces the .mjs; the cursor is a commit sha in `docs/ops/NOTIFIED.md`, the job checks out the tip of main, is serialised, commits the cursor with GITHUB_TOKEN + [skip ci] after 2xx and fails visibly on a refused send; workflow via `docs/ci/notify-owner.yml`.

items.title: A relay round survives a stalled host: fetch-relay.mjs writes meta.json and the bodies after every line (not at the end), gives HEAD and GET a 30 s timeout, and after three consecutive timeouts on one host marks that host’s remaining lines `skipped: host stalled` instead of waiting 90 s on each

Writing the response files incrementally and committing whatever landed (the Commit step runs `if: always()` with the skip-ci marker) turns a dead round into a partial one with the stall recorded per line (`timeout` status, elapsed ms); the host-level skip after three consecutive timeouts bounds a one-host round at ≈ 90 s; HEAD/GET at 30 s (RENDER keeps 90 s) catches a stalled server in a third of the time. Tests on the pure parts (fetch-relay-lines.ts: the skip decision, the per-line record). Reading 10-26 19:28 (burn-down, gankdat sitemap-5xx-read): the host never stalled — the lines were 503s. A gankdat stats page whose blob is missing answers 503 with `Retry-After: 3600`, and fetchOne retries 429/503 three times after min(Retry-After, 30 s), so each such line costs ~95 s before it is recorded; 70 lines of which 46 were 503 is 70+ minutes, both 10-26 rounds died at the 12-minute step with nothing written.
